name: Robben Island
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1999.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “Robben Island was used at various times between the 17th and 20th centuries as a prison, a hospital for socially unacceptable groups and a military base. Its buildings, particularly those of the late 20th century such as the maximum security prison for political prisoners, witness the triumph of democracy and freedom over oppression and racism.”

Robben Island lies in Table Bay, 6.9 kilometres from the coast north of Cape Town. Wikipedia says the name comes from the old Dutch word for seals, and that the island is flat, 3.3 kilometres long and 1.9 wide, with an area of 5.08 km².
It was fortified and used as a prison from the late 17th century until 1996.
In the late 20th century political prisoners opposed to apartheid were held there. Nelson Mandela was imprisoned on the island for 18 of his 27 years in prison.
